arguments: You are an independent source-grounded red-team reviewer. Use no tools. Output the requested JSON only.

attacks.title: Same-turn amount/date completion rows give different results depending on row order
attacks.assessment: TRUE FAULT, from grammar-conforming input. The first turn is handled correctly: a complete amount plus an unfinished ordinal date with u=date keeps a=213 and asks only for the date. The fault appears on the next turn, when the customer sends a date row and a changed-amount row as separate complete rows, which the contract requires. If the date row comes first, it agrees 213 on 16 Oct. The amount row then reopens the product as a dateless pending, so the agent asks for the date again and the just-given date is dropped. If the amount row comes first, the product agrees 250 on 16 Oct. The same facts in a different order produce different state.
source_references: controller L437-456 (pending: a kept, d popped, need=[date])
controller L493 (requires not p.pending, which was just popped at L503)
raw_turns: T1: I can pay 213 on the sixteenth...
T2a: On 16 October. Actually make it 250.
literal_event_rows:
k=proposal|c=1|p=personal loan|d=16 October
k=proposal|c=1|p=personal loan|a=250
END

k=proposal|c=1|p=personal loan|a=250
k=proposal|c=1|p=personal loan|d=16 October
END
attacks.setup: Verified customer. One personal_loan with past_due >= 250, floor <= 213, late band. now=2026-10-14 (Wed), so 16 Oct is a business day before the deadline. Phase is collect after the get_account statement.
attacks.producer_conformance: All rows are advertised grammar. The c=0 row with u=date is literal_example L80. Amount-only and date-only completion rows are L82-83. Separate rows are required by the prompt's 'Different amounts/dates REQUIRE separate rows'.
attacks.failure_path: T1: L437. pending={a:'213',need:[date],incomplete}. The state serialized at L535 includes the pending. T2a, row 1: L481. need={date}, d is added, need becomes empty, and a=213 is recorded as agreed at L515 (pending popped at L503). Row 2: pending={} and need is empty, but d is missing. L493 fails because 'd' is not in e. L495-496 sets pending={a:'250',need:[]} and status=open. L520 advance then asks 'Please finish the exact date', so 16 Oct is lost. T2b, row 1: a=250 overwrites the cached amount, need={date} stays, so it remains pending. Row 2 completes it as agreed 250 on 2026-10-16. The readback at L176, the consent at L412, and the body at L203 then carry 250 and 2026-10-16.
attacks.expected_observable: T2a: the agent says 'Please finish the exact date for your personal loan.' T2b: the agent reads back 'personal loan, 250.00 on 2026-10-16. Do you confirm?'
attacks.positive_control: T1 alone correctly asks only for the date and does not record 213 as agreed. Single-row completion (L83) produces an agreed 213 on 2026-10-16. A bare 'sixteenth' row with c=1 is a different case: dateval returns None, which goes through the vague path at L499-502 and consumes the one vague ask. That is not a crash.
attacks.witness_plan: Use a local harness with the controller exec'd under a stubbed vars. Feed T1, then T2a or T2b. Diff s.products[0] and the dialogue_line.
attacks.claim_limit: Source trace only. The failure is a lost or re-asked date, not an invalid write. Every write is still guarded at L202.

attacks.title: A delayed refusal_pending overrides later valid terms for the same product
attacks.assessment: TRUE FAULT, from grammar-conforming input. A refusal on product A is held while sibling B's pending date is collected. When the customer later volunteers valid terms for A, L515 sets status=agreed but never clears refusal_pending. Then L522 pops the flag and calls persuade(A). That reopens A with a past_due offer for Friday and uses up a persuasion attempt. This breaks Brief A rule 29, which says a customer's proposal is never a refusal, and it drops the customer's amount.
raw_turns: T1: Not the credit card. For the personal loan, 213 on...
T2: The loan on 16 October. And actually I can do 100 on the card on 16 October too.
literal_event_rows:
k=proposal|c=1|p=personal loan|d=16 October
k=proposal|c=1|p=credit card|a=100|d=2026-10-16
END
attacks.setup: Verified customer. get_account order is the credit_card (floor <= 100 <= past_due) and then the personal_loan. now=2026-10-14.
attacks.failure_path: T1: the card gets refusal_pending, its offer is popped, and status=open (L461-466). The loan goes pending (L437-456). L520 advance asks for the loan date. The flag is serialized at L535. T2: the loan is agreed 213 on 2026-10-16. The card is agreed 100 on 2026-10-16 (L515), with refusal_pending still true. L519 finds no pending, so L522 pops the flag and calls persuade(card): attempts=1, a=past_due, d=2026-10-16, status=open, phase=offer. If the customer then answers k=yes|c=1|p=all, L419 limits targets to the spoken offers, so only the card is agreed at past_due. The readback at L176 and the body at L203 would then carry past_due, not 100. The customer can still see this in the readback, so it is a wrong offer rather than a silent mis-write.
attacks.expected_observable: After T2 the agent says 'Can you pay <past_due> for your credit card ending NNNN on 2026-10-16?' instead of reading back both promises.
attacks.positive_control: If T2 contains only the loan date row, the delayed persuasion of the card on its own is correct (rule 30 attempt 1). It fires after the pending date is resolved, as the comment at L465 intends.
attacks.witness_plan: Use the local harness. Feed T1 and T2. Assert that products[0].attempts==1, products[0].status=='open', and offer.amount==past_due.
attacks.claim_limit: Source trace only. Fix proposal 1 addresses it. No ledger claim is made.

attacks.title: A 'yes, no problem' consent loops on readback; qualified yes and admin+security answer are positive controls
attacks.assessment: MIXED. TRUE FAULT (liveness, from grammar-conforming input): the negation regex at L394 matches 'no' or 'not' inside an affirmative confirmation, so a clean k=confirm|c=1|p=all falls through to L413. At L477 it re-agrees the same terms. Then L524 advance re-reads them back with no consent. Each honest repeat loops until the call ends through the safe_exit path, either on turns>70 (L279) or on max_node_turns via max_turn_transition. Under the control flow traced here, no wrong write occurs. REPAIRED/POSITIVE: 'Yes, but the 19th' is a correction (L394 blocks it, and the L482 pending route re-validates). Also, an answer row carrying admin=purpose with v present still verifies (L361), and the admin prefix is deferred to the next spoken line (L526-529).
source_references: controller L245-248 (verified only from a receipt-matched all_verified)
raw_turns: Confirm: Yes, no problem, I confirm.
Correction control: Yes, but make it 19 October.
DOB phase: Why are you calling? It's the seventeenth of April 1988.
attacks.setup: Phase confirm with one or more agreed products and readback spoken. A separate run with phase dob and admin='purpose'.
attacks.producer_conformance: All rows are advertised grammar (L67, L68, L73). admin is set within the contract enum.
attacks.failure_path: Consent: L394 fails because \bno\b matches. L477 sets a and dt to the agreed values. L515 re-agrees and L422 clears consent. L524 advance, then L176 reads back again. Commit at L202 is never reached. The correction row: consent_terms is false, so L482 sets pending, the date completes to 2026-10-19 (a Monday, within the deadline), and the product is re-read back. The admin row: L361 does not count it as a decline because v is present, so route=verify_identity and the prefix goes to admin_pending. It is spoken with the next line, after the receipt.
attacks.expected_observable: The agent repeats 'Please confirm: ... Do you confirm?' after every 'yes, no problem'. For the correction, the readback shows 19 October. For the admin row, the verify_identity body is {date_of_birth, 1988-04-17}, and the next spoken line begins 'I can explain after the security check.'
attacks.positive_control: Bare k=confirm|c=1|p=all with raw 'Yes, I confirm' gives consent=readback and then create_promise.
attacks.witness_plan: Use the local harness with raw_speech variants. Count the readback repetitions and confirm that route never becomes create_promise.
attacks.claim_limit: Source-only liveness fault. The ordering of the deferred admin answer is a style issue, not a write error.

architectural_proposals: Clear refusal_pending, offer and the vague counter whenever a row places a product in agreed or pending state (at L515/L456). Process all rows of a turn into a per-product merged term before validation, so the outcome does not depend on row order.

Decide consent from the structured row only: k=confirm|c=1 with no a/d, or a/d that equal the readback. Restrict the raw-speech negation veto to the producer's c=0 or correction flag rather than a bare \bno\b match.

Add a contract value such as u=none for a trailing clause where both components are complete. Treat a bare ordinal d as a fragment that triggers a date re-ask without consuming the rule-21 vague attempt.

guard_assessments.qualified_or_stale_consent: Conservative. Qualified yes is blocked by L394 and goes to pending. Stale receipts and non-confirm turns clear consent (L240, L316, L422). The token must match the readback (L202). An honest stale receipt comes only from a mismatched request_id or a duplicate, and is handled at L227-241. Stale state can be supplied only by a malicious caller who injects state, signal or api_* as call variables (customerVariables). Those are not produced by the extractor, so that is assumed malicious state injection, outside the honest grammar. The over-strict regex causes the B10-03 liveness loop.
guard_assessments.verified_security_admin: Sound. verified is set only from a receipt-matched all_verified (L245-248). Notes and promises require verified (L202, L207). An admin question plus a complete v proceeds to verify, and purpose without v counts as a decline (L361).
guard_assessments.refusal_pending: Faulty. The flag survives a later valid agreement (B10-02).
guard_assessments.persistence_binding: Good. state is serialized at every exit (L535) and at the exception path (L540). The readback tuples round-trip through JSON as lists, which match the token list at L202. The body is baked from vars set at L203 against the floor, past_due, business-day and deadline guards.

limitations: Source review only. Nothing was executed, and no extraction, hosted run or bank ledger was observed.
Platform behaviour is inferred from the docs: the max_node_turns counter on the re-entered speak node, the number typing of the baked amount, and post-hook ordering.
Only the three prioritized areas were traced. Callback, transfer and note paths were sampled, not exhaustively reviewed.

independent_qualifications.conclusion: Independent CPU confirms date-first/amount-second same-turn row loss versus amount-first/date-second agreement. Across separate turns both completion orders converge, and complete amount plus partial 16/16th/sixteenth date retains amount 213.
independent_qualifications.producer_scope: Literal output grammar allows these rows; same-product rows in one turn are not empirically observed, and a preferred extractor could combine facts. A separate conforming clause-isolation probe finds a nonterminal raw ellipsis forces the last complete sibling incomplete (controller:L323,L437).

independent_qualifications.conclusion: Independent grammar-conforming, persisted-variable sequence reproduces agreed loan 213 on 2026-10-16 being reopened as an offer for 540 by a stale refusal_pending flag. No unauthorized write follows without a later confirmation.
independent_qualifications.persistence_scope: Fresh JSON-decoded variable dictionary on every invocation; local in-memory store only. Actual Freya persistence/re-entry semantics remain unqualified.

independent_qualifications.conclusion: Single-product Yes, no problem, I confirm repeats unchanged readback without consent. In the multi-product variant, paid siblings are reopened as fresh offers when all falls through the raw-negation veto. Two local repetitions were executed; bounded-call termination was source-traced, not platform-tested.
independent_qualifications.guard_controls: Changed date and incomplete correction block writes. Complete DOB/phone plus purpose/AI proceed through synthetic verification sequence; verified security persists. An honest mismatched receipt clears consent. Forging both state and matching receipt is explicitly a caller-contract violation, not an observed extractor or customer vulnerability.

independent_qualifications.architectural_qualification: Do not remove the raw safety veto wholesale based solely on extracted confirm. Preserve qualified/stale consent protection while adding clause-scoped correction/polarity evidence and jointly validating producer and consumer. Adding u=none requires a versioned producer/consumer change; it is not supported by B10 existing grammar. No mandatory opening, SMS sentence, judge, API or candidate changes were made.

prioritized_recommendations.recommendation: Cancel stale deferred refusal when valid fresh terms supersede it; consume only refusals still applicable to the target current disposition. Keep independently unfinished sibling need flags.

Define same-product multi-row turn semantics and assemble per-product facts before validation/transition so identical facts converge regardless of row order; reject ambiguous conflicting facts and re-read changed terms.

Scope raw incompleteness/negation to the relevant clause; preserve affirmative idioms and agreed readback target set while retaining correction, pending and fresh-consent write guards. Preserve paid/recorded dispositions.
